title: Nicolas Cage Is 62 and He Just Became Spider-Man. It Is the Best Thing on Prime Video This Week.
excerpt: Spider-Noir drops on Prime Video in black-and-white and colour. The reviews are strong. The concept is absurd. It works.
body:
Nicolas Cage is 62 years old, and he has just become Spider-Man. Not the Spider-Man you know — the one swinging through Manhattan in spandex. This Spider-Man wears a fedora, carries a revolver, and solves crimes in a version of 1930s New York that looks like it was shot through a whiskey glass. Spider-Noir landed on Prime Video this week, and it is one of the strangest, most watchable things on any streaming platform right now.

## The Premise

Cage plays Ben Reilly, a retired superhero who hung up his mask years ago and now works as a private investigator. Someone hires him on a case that forces him to confront the political corruption, organized crime, and old enemies he thought he had left behind. The show is available in two formats — black-and-white and what Amazon is calling "True-Hue" colour. Both versions are on Prime Video simultaneously, and the choice is yours.

## Why It Works

The reviews are almost unanimously positive, and they all point to the same thing: Cage is fully committed. At 62, he is calling himself "a Spider-Man for aging adults," and he means it. The wirework is there, but so is the weariness. This is not a superhero origin story. It is a noir detective drama that happens to involve a man who can climb walls.

Brendan Gleeson plays a supporting role that early reviewers are calling scene-stealing. Lamorne Morris and Li Jun Li round out a cast that understands the assignment — this is pulp fiction in the literal sense, a 1930s crime story with comic book DNA.

The dual-format release is an experiment worth paying attention to. The black-and-white version is being treated as the "canonical" aesthetic by the creators, but Amazon knows most viewers will default to colour. It is the kind of creative gamble that streaming platforms can afford to take because nobody is paying ₹300 for a theatre ticket.

## The India Connection

Spider-Noir is not Indian content, and it does not pretend to be. But it matters for the diaspora viewing conversation for two reasons.

First, Prime Video is pushing this as its tentpole for the week across every market, including India. If you have a Prime subscription — and most NRI households do — this is what the algorithm will serve you.

Second, the show's success or failure will influence how aggressively Amazon greenlights similar genre experiments. Prime Video has been investing heavily in Indian originals like Citadel: Honey Bunny, Mirzapur, and The Family Man, and its global strategy increasingly treats the Indian diaspora as a premium audience. A hit Spider-Noir proves that NRI subscribers watch global content too, which means more budget for everything.

## The Verdict

Stream it. Watch the first episode in black-and-white. If it does not hold you, switch to colour. But give Cage the first 20 minutes — the man earned it.

Spider-Noir is streaming now on Prime Video. All episodes of Season 1 are available. You do not need to have watched any Spider-Verse film to follow the story, though it helps if you appreciate a 62-year-old man punching criminals in a trench coat.
